scope_correction: These are representative host/runtime traces, not an Agency OS product composition and not a selection from any recipe.

gates.rule: Every stateful resource has exactly one authority_owner.
Every mutable resource has exactly one write_owners entry; readers and projections are not writers of canonical donor data.
Every physical schema/table has one migration_owner or explicitly declares that the external provider owns DDL.
Tenant/workspace/client scope and the enforcement mechanism are explicit and negative-tested; a tenant_id column alone is insufficient.
Cross-owner reads use typed APIs, qualified read roles, mappings or events; shared-table mutation is forbidden.
Every event-fed projection has one writer, a source cursor/idempotency key and a replay/rebuild path.
The database stores only secret references and metadata; plaintext credentials never enter data, logs, events or model context.
Backup, deletion, retention, restore and forward-repair owners are named for each stateful resource.

stateful_resources.notes: Stable principals and service identities; email is an attribute, never the durable key.
Employee, team and client-account memberships are explicit relations; team membership is not blanket visibility.
Block settings are registrations; donor-private settings remain donor-owned.
One route owner and one launcher owner; contextual secondary navigation may remain inside a module.
Append-only identity, policy, setting, migration, release and recovery receipts; payloads are minimized and secret-free.
Canonical-to-external mappings use opaque IDs and are the only join surface between independent module stores.
Signed/versioned envelopes are persisted before acknowledgement; duplicate event IDs are no-ops.
Derived activity is replayable and never becomes a second writer for a block's canonical record.
Connection metadata is host-scoped even if provider catalogue/OAuth mechanics are reused.
Only references and rotation metadata are in the host data plane; plaintext secret material is external.
Placeholder owned resource for traces; a future product must replace it with a named domain resource.
The donor keeps its native data and migration history; host joins through typed APIs/events/mappings.
Object bytes and metadata have an explicit namespace; links use short-lived scoped URLs.
Search is rebuildable derived state and must apply authorization filters before returning results.

representative_traces.shape: intact service behind a host adapter
contract_path: host inbox and idempotent read-model projection

host_bindings.identity: host issues a short-lived audience-bound handoff; donor creates only its native session.
host_bindings.authority: host and donor policies intersect; the adapter cannot grant an unapproved donor role.
host_bindings.navigation: host owns the launcher and route; the service may own contextual secondary navigation.
host_bindings.data: donor.native-records is canonical; integration.external-refs and read-model.activity are host-owned derived resources.
host_bindings.recovery: service can be disabled and routed to a typed unavailable surface without mutating host truth.

scope.notes: Arithmetic fixture only; not a selected donor or production capacity claim.

managed_dependencies.notes: One managed cluster is the default where schema/role/migration compatibility passes; plan capacity is not measured here.
Used for distributed leases/queues when more than one runtime instance exists.
Backend limits, retention and price remain unknown until selected.

refusal_conditions.rule: Any calculated capacity inequality is false.
A stateful resource has more than one writer or migration owner.
A mutable physical resource has no named migration owner.
Queue work exceeds worker concurrency or side effects lack a bounded contract.
Plaintext secret material enters the data, event, log, browser or model plane.
A required release, schema, projection, connector or external effect has no recovery action.
A process, active-memory, connection, worker, upgrade or rollback factor is >= 4.5 while confidence is < 0.75.
At least one burden factor has confidence below 0.75.
A donor creates schemas/tables at runtime or has an unqualified namespace assumption.
A managed dependency limit or cost is plan-specific or unmeasured.
A write/message provider effect is not atomically reversible.

falsifiers: A service cannot accept host context without retaining a second unrestricted login authority.
Donor canonical records require host writes or shared-table mutation to answer a cross-module question.
Measured p95/p99 service or worker resources exceed this fixture after the declared reserve.

representative_traces.shape: bounded package plus static microfrontend mount

host_bindings.identity: the module consumes the host principal and never ships an independent signup/login route.
host_bindings.authority: the module receives only the host-scoped capability set; a UI mount cannot grant data access.
host_bindings.navigation: host owns the top-level route and launcher; module-local tabs are contextual.
host_bindings.data: the package may call a host-owned typed port; a static bundle has no direct database or secret access.
host_bindings.recovery: the host error boundary and feature flag can disable the mount while preserving the rest of the host.

scope.notes: Arithmetic fixture only; the static mount intentionally has zero additional listeners.

managed_dependencies.notes: The package calls a typed port; the host owns the database boundary.
Telemetry capacity is not part of this local process fixture.

representative_traces.shape: typed engine service plus pooled worker and scheduler

host_bindings.identity: the engine receives a scoped service identity and actor/context metadata, not a browser session or reusable credential.
host_bindings.authority: actions are typed as read/write/message and bounded by approval, idempotency and egress policy.
host_bindings.navigation: the engine has no implied global route; any UI is a separate host/module registration.
host_bindings.data: the engine owns only its declared resource or provider state; host projections own derived views.
host_bindings.recovery: jobs pause/replay only when idempotent; prior engine image/config and projection cursor are retained.

scope.notes: Arithmetic fixture only; external action latency, provider limits and engine semantics remain unmeasured.

managed_dependencies.notes: The engine may use a same-cluster schema only after the compatibility and migration-owner gates pass.
Distributed queue/lease behavior must be selected and measured before multi-instance use.
Provider retention and cost are not measured.
Provider rate limits, latency, callback completion and refresh behavior remain provider-specific unknowns.
